sources.text: Recursive self-improvement compounds through the algorithmic link, and AI4AI-Bench is built to measure that link on its own: ten frozen research repositories, each asking an agent to improve the training algorithm it already applies to its own model, with four hours to write code, twelve to run what was written, and an evaluation the agent never sees. Across 29 configurations of six systems on all ten tasks the mean score is 0.166on a scale where the algorithm the repository already ships is0.1and the task optimum is1.0, and the best system reaches0.250. The submissions say where the rest of that distance went: of the 263 that changed anything, 141 never touch how the model learns at all, and the 122 that do average0.226against 0.126for the rest — the algorithmic layer is where the distance is closed, and most submissions never go to it. More reasoning effort mostly buys the willingness to go, taking that minority from8%of submissions to64% and the mean score from0.094to0 .196, which still leaves the strongest setting a tenth of the way past the algorithm it started from. What today’s agents do at the algorithmic link, then, is recover a competent default rather than design past one; whether that changes is the measurement this benchmark exists to keep taking.

sources.text: AI4AI-Bench: Benchmarking LLM Agents in Algorithmic Design for Recursive Self-Improvement Yizhe Chi, Wenyi Li, Deyao Hong, Xiaoqiu Wang, Mingju Gao, Kaisen Yang, Bingxiang He, Youjie Zheng, Calvin Xiao, Qinhuai Na Navers Lab, Einsia.AI Tsinghua University Project Lead Corresponding Author Abstract.Recursive self-improvement (RSI) asks whether an AI system can improve the process that produces AI systems, so that the next system inherits the improvement. That process is the training algorithm: a better objective or update rule improves the compute-capability exchange rate for every subsequent run, including the one that produces the next agent. Whether RSI is feasible therefore turns on whether an agent can design training algorithms. No benchmark isolates that ability: existing suites are won by collecting data or by tuning hyperparameters, and none tells a change to how a run is executed apart from a change to how the model learns. We present AI4AI-Bench, 10 frozen research repositories spanning 10 training algorithm families. In each task, an agent has 4 hours on one B300 to rewrite the training algorithm; its code is then rerun from scratch for up to 12 hours and scored by a fixed evaluator hidden from the agent, against the repository’s original algorithm under the same procedure. Because the 10 metrics are incommensurable, every task is mapped onto one scale on which0is an uninformative model,0.1is the algorithm the repository ships, and1.0 is the task optimum. # KPMG Research Executive Brief

## Stakeholder Persona
Allison Tatterson

## Question
How are the incommensurable AI4AI-Bench task metrics normalized?

## Confidence Tier & Rationale
Moderate (70% evidence score)

Moderate: retrieval scores were not saved and contribute zero. Weights: retrieval 30%, citation coverage 30%, quote/numeric checks 25%, source diversity 15%. This evidence indicator does not verify meaning, answer completeness or business outcomes; human review is required.

## What the Study Found
The incommensurable AI4AI-Bench task metrics are normalized onto one scale where 0 is an uninformative model, 0.1 is the algorithm the repository ships, and 1.0 is the task optimum. [3]

Evidence:
- "ten tasks the mean score is 0.166on a scale where the algorithm the repository already ships is0.1and the task optimum is1.0, and the best" [3]

## Why It Matters to KPMG
Proposed Advisory applications for stakeholder review: AI4AI-Bench distinguishes hyperparameter/compute tuning from true learning-method innovation, informing KPMG AI engineering evaluation. [3] The papers do not establish KPMG-specific outcomes or ROI.

## What KPMG Could Consider
Pilot clean baseline reruns and held-out evaluations the agent cannot influence; inspect algorithm changes separately from compute and hyperparameter changes. [3] Consider a small, reversible pilot on representative, approved public data. Compare against the current baseline for quality, cost and latency; require human-in-the-loop review of every claim before stakeholder use. Sample-size and methodological limitations: use only the populations, tasks and benchmarks described in the cited evidence; any unstated sample size or method detail remains unknown. Do not generalize benchmark gains to client outcomes without independent validation. [3] Apply the selected stakeholder's review priorities without relaxing evidence checks.

## Validation Status
Mechanical checks passed; interpretation and completeness need human review.
